---
title: "Asset Pricing — Kernel, Constrained (Uno)"
---

## Setup

[JAX](https://docs.jax.dev) underlies everything below: array math via `jax.numpy`, [compilation](https://docs.jax.dev/en/latest/jit-compilation.html) via `jax.jit`, and exact derivatives via [automatic differentiation](https://docs.jax.dev/en/latest/automatic-differentiation.html) — the solver differentiates the residual program itself, so no derivative is coded by hand. JAX defaults to 32-bit floats, so we switch on 64-bit and the most accurate matmul *before* creating any array, then import everything we need.

This notebook solves the same problem as the companion ridgeless notebook, but with a **constrained optimizer**: the interior-point solver [Uno](https://github.com/cvanaret/Uno) through `unopy`, with JAX supplying the gradient, Jacobian, and Hessian callbacks. The model code — `p`, `dividends`, `residual_fn`, and `theta_0` — is the ridgeless notebook's, retyped verbatim; here `p` is only a value container, since the NLP solver is host-side C++ and nothing differentiates through it.

```{python}
import jax

jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True)
jax.config.update("jax_default_matmul_precision", "highest")

import time

import jax.numpy as jnp
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import unopy
from jax.flatten_util import ravel_pytree
```

Structural parameters of the economic model.

```{python}
r = 0.1  # interest rate
c = 0.02  # dividend flow constant
g = -0.2  # dividend growth rate
x_0 = 0.01  # initial dividend
p = {"r": r, "c": c, "g": g, "x_0": x_0}
```

Parameters of the algorithm: the kernel hyperparameters and the collocation and test grids.

```{python}
ELL = 10.0  # Matern-1/2 length scale
SIGMA = 1.0  # kernel amplitude
TRAIN_T = 40.0
N_TRAIN = 41
TEST_T = 50.0
N_TEST = 100
N_VALIDATION = 201
TRAIN_RESIDUAL = 1e-8
VALIDATION_RESIDUAL = 1e-4

t_train = jnp.linspace(0.0, TRAIN_T, N_TRAIN)
t_test = jnp.linspace(0.0, TEST_T, N_TEST)
t_validation = jnp.linspace(0.0, TRAIN_T, N_VALIDATION)
```

## The model

An asset pays the deterministic dividend flow

$$
x(t) = \left(x_0 + \frac{c}{g}\right) e^{g t} - \frac{c}{g},
$$

and no-arbitrage at interest rate $r$ prices it by the linear ODE $p'(t) = r\, p(t) - x(t)$. Every solution is the fundamental price plus a bubble $\zeta e^{rt}$; as in the ridgeless notebook we impose no boundary condition — the minimum-norm selection below rules out the explosive mode, with the initial price $p_0$ a free unknown.

## The integrated kernel

The hypothesis class is an RKHS built from the Matérn-1/2 kernel applied to the *derivative* of the price path,

$$
k(t, t') = \sigma^2 e^{-|t - t'|/\ell},
\qquad
h(d) = \sigma^2 \ell \left(1 - e^{-d/\ell}\right),
\qquad
\tilde K(t_i, t_j) = h(t_j) + \operatorname{sign}(t_i - t_j)\, h(|t_i - t_j|),
$$

so that $p(t) = p_0 + \sum_j \alpha_j \tilde K(t, t_j)$ with the exact derivative $p'(t) = \sum_j \alpha_j k(t, t_j)$, and $\tilde K(0, \cdot) = 0$ makes $p_0$ the initial price. The stacked no-arbitrage residual $p'(t_i) - \big(r\, p(t_i) - x(t_i)\big)$ is the ridgeless notebook's `residual_fn`, verbatim.

```{python}
def antiderivative(d):
    return SIGMA**2 * ELL * (1.0 - jnp.exp(-d / ELL))


def kernel_matrices(t_i, t_j):
    s = t_i[:, None] - t_j[None, :]
    K = SIGMA**2 * jnp.exp(-jnp.abs(s) / ELL)
    K_tilde = antiderivative(t_j)[None, :] + jnp.sign(s) * antiderivative(jnp.abs(s))
    return K, K_tilde


def dividends(t, p):
    return (p["x_0"] + p["c"] / p["g"]) * jnp.exp(p["g"] * t) - p["c"] / p["g"]


def residual_fn(theta, args, p):
    alpha, p_0 = theta["alpha"], theta["p_0"]
    price = p_0 + args["K_tilde"] @ alpha
    return args["K"] @ alpha - (p["r"] * price - dividends(args["t"], p))
```

## The constrained program

The ridgeless notebook reaches the minimum-norm interpolant as the $\lambda \to 0$ limit of the penalized least squares $\min \|r\|^2 + \lambda\, \alpha^\top K \alpha$. The constrained-optimizer implementation solves that limit **exactly**, as the nonlinear program

$$
\min_{\alpha,\, p_0}\ \alpha^\top K \alpha
\quad \text{s.t.} \quad
p'(t_i) - \big(r\, p(t_i) - x(t_i)\big) = 0 \quad \text{at every training date.}
$$

The equality constraints are `residual_fn` verbatim, with `ravel_pytree` flattening the ridgeless `theta_0` dict (sorted keys) into Uno's flat vector and returning the inverse `unravel`; objective, constraints, and their derivatives — `jax.grad`, [`jax.jacfwd`](https://docs.jax.dev/en/latest/automatic-differentiation.html), and the Hessian of the Lagrangian via `jax.hessian` — reach the interior-point solver as jitted callbacks.

```{python}
K, K_tilde = kernel_matrices(t_train, t_train)
args = {"K": K, "K_tilde": K_tilde, "t": t_train}

theta_0 = {"alpha": jnp.zeros(N_TRAIN), "p_0": jnp.zeros(())}
x_initial, unravel = ravel_pytree(theta_0)
N_VARIABLES = x_initial.size
N_CONSTRAINTS = N_TRAIN


@jax.jit
def objective(x):
    alpha = unravel(x)["alpha"]
    return alpha @ K @ alpha


@jax.jit
def constraints(x):
    return residual_fn(unravel(x), args, p)


def lagrangian(x, objective_multiplier, multipliers):
    return objective_multiplier * objective(x) + multipliers @ constraints(x)


objective_gradient = jax.jit(jax.grad(objective))
constraint_jacobian = jax.jit(jax.jacfwd(constraints))
lagrangian_hessian = jax.jit(jax.hessian(lagrangian, argnums=0))
```

## The NLP setup

Uno takes the problem in sparse-triplet form; with a dense kernel model the Jacobian is simply every (row, column) pair and the Hessian its lower triangle.

```{python}
variable_lower_bounds = np.full(N_VARIABLES, -np.inf)
variable_upper_bounds = np.full(N_VARIABLES, np.inf)
model = unopy.Model(
    unopy.PROBLEM_QUADRATIC,
    N_VARIABLES,
    variable_lower_bounds,
    variable_upper_bounds,
    unopy.ZERO_BASED_INDEXING,
)


def objective_callback(x):
    return float(objective(jnp.asarray(x)))


def objective_gradient_callback(x, gradient):
    gradient[:] = np.asarray(objective_gradient(jnp.asarray(x)))


model.set_objective(unopy.MINIMIZE, objective_callback, objective_gradient_callback)

jacobian_rows = np.repeat(np.arange(N_CONSTRAINTS, dtype=np.int32), N_VARIABLES)
jacobian_columns = np.tile(np.arange(N_VARIABLES, dtype=np.int32), N_CONSTRAINTS)


def constraints_callback(x, constraint_output):
    constraint_output[:] = np.asarray(constraints(jnp.asarray(x)))


def jacobian_callback(x, jacobian_output):
    jacobian_output[:] = np.asarray(constraint_jacobian(jnp.asarray(x))).reshape(-1)


model.set_constraints(
    N_CONSTRAINTS,
    constraints_callback,
    np.zeros(N_CONSTRAINTS),
    np.zeros(N_CONSTRAINTS),
    len(jacobian_rows),
    jacobian_rows,
    jacobian_columns,
    jacobian_callback,
)

hessian_rows, hessian_columns = (
    idx.astype(np.int32) for idx in np.tril_indices(N_VARIABLES)
)


def hessian_callback(x, objective_multiplier, multipliers, hessian_output):
    hessian = np.asarray(
        lagrangian_hessian(
            jnp.asarray(x), float(objective_multiplier), jnp.asarray(multipliers)
        )
    )
    hessian_output[:] = hessian[hessian_rows, hessian_columns]


model.set_lagrangian_hessian(
    len(hessian_rows),
    unopy.LOWER_TRIANGLE,
    hessian_rows,
    hessian_columns,
    hessian_callback,
)
model.set_lagrangian_sign_convention(unopy.MULTIPLIER_POSITIVE)
model.set_initial_primal_iterate(np.asarray(x_initial))
```

## Solve

The `ipopt` preset reproduces the classic filter line-search interior-point method. `primal_solution` appends solver-internal auxiliaries, so only the leading $n + 1$ block is ours.

```{python}
solver = unopy.UnoSolver()
solver.set_preset("ipopt")
solver.set_option("logger", "SILENT")
solver.set_option("print_solution", False)

start = time.perf_counter()
result = solver.optimize(model)
solve_time = time.perf_counter() - start

theta = unravel(jnp.asarray(np.array(result.primal_solution)[:N_VARIABLES]))
alpha, p_0 = theta["alpha"], theta["p_0"]
```

## Results

Identical diagnostics to the ridgeless notebook: the no-arbitrage residual on the test grid (extending past the training horizon), the learned $p_0$ against the closed-form fundamental $p_f(0) = 0.7$, and the relative pricing error against

$$
p_f(t) = \frac{x_0 + c/g}{r - g}\, e^{g t} - \frac{c}{g r}.
$$

```{python}
K_test, K_tilde_test = kernel_matrices(t_test, t_train)
price_test = p_0 + K_tilde_test @ alpha
test_residual = K_test @ alpha - (r * price_test - dividends(t_test, p))

# Closed-form fundamental (no-bubble) price.
price_fundamental = (x_0 + c / g) * jnp.exp(g * t_test) / (r - g) - c / (g * r)
rel_error = jnp.abs(price_test - price_fundamental) / price_fundamental

print(f"solve: {result.solution_status.name} in {solve_time:.2f}s (incl. jit)")
print(f"p_0 = {float(p_0):.6f}")
print(f"max |test residual|: {float(jnp.max(jnp.abs(test_residual))):.3e}")
print(f"max rel error vs fundamental: {float(jnp.max(rel_error)):.3e}")
```

The solve status above is reported for diagnostics; acceptance is judged against the max train residual bound and, with `residual_fn` reused on a finer validation grid over the training horizon, the between-node residual.

```{python}
max_train_residual = float(jnp.max(jnp.abs(residual_fn(theta, args, p))))
K_validation, K_tilde_validation = kernel_matrices(t_validation, t_train)
args_validation = {"K": K_validation, "K_tilde": K_tilde_validation, "t": t_validation}
validation_residual = residual_fn(theta, args_validation, p)
max_validation_residual = float(jnp.max(jnp.abs(validation_residual)))
mean_validation_residual = float(jnp.mean(jnp.abs(validation_residual)))
train_ok = max_train_residual <= TRAIN_RESIDUAL
validation_ok = mean_validation_residual <= VALIDATION_RESIDUAL
print(
    f"max train residual {max_train_residual:.3e} <= {TRAIN_RESIDUAL:.0e}: {train_ok}"
)
print(
    f"mean validation residual {mean_validation_residual:.3e} <= "
    f"{VALIDATION_RESIDUAL:.0e}: {validation_ok}"
)
print(f"max validation residual {max_validation_residual:.3e}")
print(f"accepted: {train_ok and validation_ok}")
```

The constrained solution tracks the closed-form fundamental with no bubble. As in the ridgeless notebook the residual vanishes at the training dates and oscillates between them, so the right panel is off-grid collocation error rather than extrapolation past the horizon (dotted).

```{python}
fig, (ax_p, ax_r) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 4))
ax_p.plot(t_test, price_test, "C0", label="kernel price")
ax_p.plot(t_test, price_fundamental, "k--", label="fundamental")
ax_p.axvline(TRAIN_T, color="0.3", linestyle=":", label="train horizon")
ax_p.set(xlabel="t", ylabel="price", title="price vs fundamental")
ax_p.legend(fontsize=8)
ax_r.plot(t_test, test_residual, "C0")
ax_r.axhline(0.0, color="k", linestyle="--", linewidth=0.8)
ax_r.axvline(TRAIN_T, color="0.3", linestyle=":")
ax_r.set(xlabel="t", ylabel="residual", title="no-arbitrage residual")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
